what_happened: Research found that deliverables 1 and 6 of the 6-deliverable dispatch are already fully implemented by task 610 (batch-of-one deferral, entry guards) and task 650 (owed-sweep discharge), and that deliverable 5's declaration surface (verification_scope.closing_gate) is already reserved by name in repo-level-declarations.md -- substantially narrowing the plan's real scope to deliverables 2, 3, 4, and populating 5.

context/standards/repo-level-declarations.md:159 contains a dangling cross-reference '(see Decisions Settled below)' pointing to a heading that does not exist anywhere in that file -- a documentation gap relevant to this task's own deliverable 5 implementation.

Two prose surfaces beyond those the research report enumerated still misdescribed the shipped batch-of-one deferral: batch-gate-stage.md's invariance paragraph states the current design but in version-relative phrasing the no-record-versioning rule forbids under agent-system/**, and orchestrate-batch-results-template.md still claims the batch-gate result is absent on a single-task batch. The research report had concluded no Deliverable 1 edit was owed; both were folded into Phase 1 instead.

The research report's five settled Decisions (tier vocabulary option (a), the ^FINDING emission contract, Deliverable 3 resolved by observation, the red-close record floor, attributed-cause-only status binding) were directly adoptable with no re-litigation, cutting planning to a scope-confirmation pass plus phase decomposition.
git-commit-phase.sh dropped 'agent-system/extensions/core/docs/guides/user-guide.md' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.

Phase 2's Scope Hypothesis widened to include docs/guides/user-guide.md (a 6th stale-framing hit beyond the plan's declared 5-surface hypothesis). git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check correctly dropped it from the phase commit since it is outside the task's declared file_scope, deposited it into proposed_file_scope, and a scoped follow-up commit via git-commit-scoped.sh landed it cleanly.

Phase 4's verify-touched.sh run (56 selected suites, interface tier) reported test-lint-state-writer-boundary.sh as a NEW failure under heavy concurrent multi-session load (impl-607/impl-610 also running full batteries). Re-ran the suite standalone twice (bare and scoped to orchestrate-close-status-bind.sh) immediately after: 28/28 and 0/0-violations clean both times. Confirmed load-induced flake, not a real regression from Phase 4's edits -- matches the contention-induced false-red incident class this task's own OWNER RULING context describes.
